# MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 Calibration checks - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
This document defines calibration check activities and acceptance criteria for instrumentation and control elements associated with Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3. It is intended for maintenance technicians and process engineers performing pre-shift and in-service verification of measurement and timing functions that impact quench control and lubricant application interfaces. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HT03 for full equipment history and drawings and to SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-03 for operational and safety procedures that bound these checks.

Background and rationale
Calibration checks confirm that control signals, sensors, and timing logic operate within acceptable behavior before parts are processed. The focus for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 is on the quench timing chain and auxiliary sensors that influence quench initiation. A failure in timing or sensor drift can result in nonconforming heat treat outcomes; timely verification mitigates production risk and reduces rework. The quench delay parameter and lubrication interfaces are high priority because they directly affect part microstructure and machine reliability.

Tools
- Reference calibrator or signal source appropriate to the instrument type
- Portable multimeter rated for the control system voltages
- Clean, lint-free cloth and approved solvent per SOP-P1-L4-02
- Manufacturer diagnostic interface or programming cable as required
- Notebook or electronic maintenance record entry per plant practice
- Approved lubricant identified in system documentation

Procedure
Overview: Perform a sequence of visual, functional, and signal verification checks while the furnace is in a safe state as described in SOP-P1-L4-02 and with lockout/tagout applied per SOP-P1-L4-03. Record all observations and test values in the equipment maintenance record.

Preparation
- Confirm work authorization and that the furnace is in the safe condition required by SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-03.
- Inspect wiring and connector housings for physical damage, loose connections, or contamination that could affect signals. Clean per approved procedure if contamination is present.
- Verify the lubricant supply and fittings for the lubrication system are present and free of leaks. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is CFW-LUB-231.

Calibration check steps
- Visual and mechanical inspection: Check sensor mounting and alignment for slippage or movement that may alter signal quality. Tighten or secure mounts if required.
- Sensor zero and span confirmation: Using the reference calibrator, inject known reference signals and observe the controller and readback. Confirm the readback follows the injected signal trend without erratic jumps.
- Timing and logic verification: Initiate the test routine in diagnostic mode and monitor the control sequence that leads to quench initiation. Use trace logging or the diagnostic interface to capture the sequence events and confirm predictable behavior.
- Quench delay verification: Observe the measured delay between the command to initiate quench and the actual actuation event in the control logs or diagnostic output. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. If the measured delay exceeds this parameter, follow corrective actions in MM-P1-L4-HT03 and coordinate with process engineering for disposition.
- Lubrication interface check: Confirm that any lubrication interlocks or sensors that affect heat treat cycles report correctly to the controller. Verify linkage continuity and signal integrity back to the input modules.

Examples and expected behavior
- Example diagnostic trace: When a simulated quench command appears in the diagnostic interface, the control logic should sequence through pre-actuation checks, open any required valves or actuators, and issue the actuation command. The event timestamps should show the actuation event within the quench delay maximum allowed. If an actuator shows repeated attempts without response, tag the actuator for repair and document findings.
- Example lubrication confirmation: When the lubrication system is exercised in manual mode, flow or presence sensors should change state and report to the controller. The controller should allow cycle progression only when sensor states meet required conditions.

Acceptance criteria
- Sensors return stable, repeatable readbacks that track injected reference signals within normal operational variance documented in MM-P1-L4-HT03.
- Control logic initiates quench actuation and other control outputs without anomalous intermediate states. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.
- Lubrication presence and interlock sensors report correctly and the lubrication system is free of leaks; lubricant in use is identified as CFW-LUB-231.
- Any deviation from the above criteria requires immediate tagging of the affected item out of service and notification to maintenance supervision and process engineering. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HT03 for escalation and repair workflows.

Records to keep
- Complete the equipment maintenance record entry with date, technician initials, diagnostic trace files, and any screenshots or exported log files. Link all entries to MM-P1-L4-HT03 records.
- Document any corrective actions taken, parts replaced, or field adjustments made. When lubrication reservoir or fittings are serviced, note the lubricant part number used: CFW-LUB-231.
- Retain a copy of the diagnostic output that demonstrates the quench timing measurement, and archive it in the maintenance system per plant document control practice.

Notes and references
- Follow all applicable lockout/tagout and safety protocols in SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-03 before performing any checks that require access to live control cabinets or actuators.
- For repair parts, calibration procedures, or further diagnostic routines not contained in this check sheet, consult MM-P1-L4-HT03.

Revision history
- Rev D: Current release. See MM-P1-L4-HT03 for equipment history and prior revision detail.
